meta.scope: Taiwan Batch 14 — Sub-national / municipal / island densification. Answers the geography question and substantially raises the municipal and spatial edge density. Covers the six special municipalities, key high-tech and peripheral counties, outlying island groups (Penghu, Kinmen, Matsu), science-park geography, local income rankings, and the structural concentration pattern. Aims for high node count where official statistical or recurring-citation material is available.
meta.strategy_note: Taiwan is primarily one main island (Formosa) plus several outlying island groups under ROC administration (Penghu, Kinmen, Matsu, and smaller holdings). Administratively it is organised into 6 special municipalities + 13 counties + 3 provincial-level cities (22 primary divisions). DGBAS does not publish full county/city GDP, but local income, population, science-park and industrial statistics support a dense spatial layer.

candidates.title: Administrative divisions of Taiwan — 6 special municipalities, 13 counties, 3 cities
candidates.description: The de-facto primary sub-national structure: six special municipalities (New Taipei, Taichung, Kaohsiung, Taipei, Taoyuan, Tainan), thirteen counties, and three provincial-level cities. Provinces are nominal; the 22 divisions are the operational units of local government and statistics.
referenced_by: Regional contrast and population concentration nodes
candidates.notes: Foundational spatial-structure node. Necessary before individual municipality or county nodes can be properly situated.

candidates.title: Six special municipalities — population and economic concentration core
candidates.description: The six special municipalities (New Taipei, Taichung, Kaohsiung, Taipei, Taoyuan, Tainan) together contain roughly 70 % of Taiwan’s population and the large majority of high-value economic activity. They form the primary core of the spatial hierarchy.
candidates.notes: Reinforces and expands the earlier regional-contrast node with explicit municipality-level framing.

candidates.title: Taipei City — capital and financial/administrative centre
candidates.publisher: Taipei City Government / DGBAS local indicators
candidates.description: Capital special municipality. Highest population density, major financial and administrative functions, and consistently among the highest household disposable-income jurisdictions.
candidates.notes: Primary administrative and financial municipal node.

candidates.title: New Taipei City — largest-population special municipality
candidates.description: Most populous special municipality (over 4 million). Functions as the broad residential and mixed industrial hinterland of the Taipei basin.

candidates.title: Taoyuan City — airport, logistics and northern industrial corridor
candidates.description: Special municipality that contains Taiwan’s main international airport and significant industrial and logistics capacity linking the Taipei basin to the Hsinchu high-tech zone.
referenced_by: Northern industrial corridor and science-park labour sheds

candidates.title: Hsinchu City and Hsinchu County — highest-income high-tech cluster
candidates.publisher: DGBAS local income statistics / Science Park administrations
candidates.description: The Hsinchu area (city + county) consistently ranks at or near the top of household disposable-income rankings, driven by the Hsinchu Science Park and the surrounding semiconductor ecosystem. Distinct from the six special municipalities but central to the high-tech spatial structure.
candidates.notes: Highest-income and purest high-tech geographic node. Critical for the dual-structure and social-impact stories.

candidates.title: Taichung City — central Taiwan industrial and population centre
candidates.description: Second- or third-largest special municipality by population; major central industrial, commercial and residential hub. Contains the Central Taiwan Science Park.

candidates.title: Tainan City — southern historical and industrial centre
candidates.description: Southern special municipality with historical significance and growing high-tech and industrial presence linked to the Southern Taiwan Science Park corridor.
referenced_by: Southern Taiwan Science Park and S-corridor expansion
candidates.notes: Southern municipal node that participates in the semiconductor southward expansion.

candidates.title: Kaohsiung City — southern port, industrial and population centre
candidates.description: Major southern special municipality, principal port, heavy-industrial base and significant population centre. Increasingly linked to the southern semiconductor and high-tech expansion.
referenced_by: Southern Science Park and industrial expansion
candidates.notes: Southern port and industrial municipal node.

candidates.title: Eastern and peripheral counties — lower density, faster ageing
candidates.publisher: DGBAS / Ministry of the Interior local statistics
candidates.description: Counties such as Hualien, Taitung, Chiayi, Yunlin, Nantou and others that exhibit lower population density, higher ageing rates, and weaker high-tech presence. Form the primary periphery against the special-municipality and Hsinchu cores.
candidates.notes: Periphery pole of the core–periphery spatial structure.

candidates.title: Penghu County / Penghu Islands
candidates.publisher: Penghu County Government / Ministry of the Interior
candidates.description: Island county in the Taiwan Strait comprising the Penghu (Pescadores) archipelago. Distinct geographic, demographic and strategic profile from the main island.

candidates.title: Kinmen County / Kinmen Islands
candidates.description: Island county lying immediately offshore from Xiamen (Fujian). Unique historical, demographic and cross-strait proximity profile; subject of distinct civil–military and exchange arrangements.

candidates.title: Lienchiang County / Matsu Islands
candidates.description: Northern outlying island group (Matsu) administered as Lienchiang County. Small population, strategic location, and distinct local statistics.

candidates.title: Outlying islands statistical and administrative set (Penghu, Kinmen, Matsu and related)
candidates.publisher: Ministry of the Interior / local governments / MAC-related where relevant
candidates.description: Collective statistical and administrative treatment of the major inhabited outlying island groups under ROC control. Distinct from the main island in demography, economy, defence posture and, in the cases of Kinmen and Matsu, cross-strait proximity.
referenced_by: Individual Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu nodes
candidates.notes: Meta-node for the island geography that answers the user’s ‘bunch of islands’ question with statistical precision.

candidates.title: County and city household disposable-income rankings
candidates.description: Annual rankings of average household disposable income by county and city. Hsinchu City (and often Hsinchu County) and Taipei regularly occupy the top positions, illustrating the spatial income consequences of the high-tech cluster.
referenced_by: Hsinchu City/County and Taipei City nodes
candidates.notes: Key quantitative bridge from the industrial geography to the social dualism story.

candidates.title: Science-park geographic system (Hsinchu, Central, Southern and related sites)
candidates.publisher: National Science and Technology Council / Science Park Bureaus
candidates.description: The formal science-park system as a spatial-industrial hierarchy: Hsinchu as the historic and still-central core, Central Taiwan Science Park, Southern Taiwan Science Park (fastest recent growth), and associated sites. Anchors the high-tech geography of the island.
referenced_by: Individual park revenue and employment statistics
candidates.notes: Geographic backbone of the semiconductor spatial structure.

candidates.title: Northern high-tech corridor and southern S-corridor expansion
candidates.publisher: Derived from science-park, industrial and municipal statistics
candidates.description: Relational spatial node describing the traditional northern concentration (Taipei–Taoyuan–Hsinchu) and the deliberate southward expansion of semiconductor and high-tech capacity into the Tainan–Kaohsiung area (S-corridor).
referenced_by: Science-park geography and Southern Science Park statistics
Municipal nodes along the western corridor
Industrial production and investment location analysis
candidates.notes: Dynamic spatial edge that captures both historical concentration and policy-driven rebalancing.

candidates.title: Taiwan sub-national spatial structure meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from MOI, DGBAS, NSTC and local government sources
candidates.description: Meta-node that integrates the administrative division structure, six special municipalities, Hsinchu high-income cluster, eastern/peripheral counties, outlying island groups, science-park geography, local income rankings, and north–south corridor dynamics into a coherent sub-national layer. Raises the internal spatial edge density of the Taiwan hub.
referenced_by: All detailed municipal, county, island and science-park nodes in this batch
candidates.notes: Integrating node so the force layout treats Taiwan’s internal geography as a dense, multi-polar structure rather than a single national point.
